column3: Close to the Greek; “fall away” is rendered “be made to stumble.”
NKJV has “this cup … pass away from Me,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “if this cannot pass.”
NKJV renders “Sleep later on and take your rest” as a question, “Are you still sleeping and resting?”; the Greek may be read either way.
NKJV has “why have you come?”; the Greek ἐφ᾽ ὃ πάρει is elliptical (“for what you are here”), and its meaning is uncertain.
Close to the Greek; “call upon” is rendered “pray to.”
NKJV has “with you,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “Every day in the temple I sat teaching.”
Close to the Greek; “guards” is rendered “servants.”
NKJV includes “the elders,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “the chief priests and the whole council.”
NKJV follows the Textus Receptus, which repeats “they found none” and names “two false witnesses”; the critical text has “but found none, though many false witnesses came; at last two came.”
